_status: Web demo for the 'layers' slide. Ten everyday attacks against the deck's three layers, in its order: people, process, technology (email filtering, phishing-resistant MFA, least privilege, offline backups). Each attack is caught by the first switched-on layer, left to right, that can catch it. Which layer catches which attack is a teaching simplification, not a measurement. Invented office, names and addresses (198.51.100.x is a documentation range).

layers.label: Staff who recognize tricks and report without fear
Routines that do not depend on one person being fooled
Tools that block or limit the damage

scenes.title: No layers
scenes.text: Ten everyday attacks on the RSSO. With nothing in the way, every one of them lands.

scenes.title: People: staff who recognize tricks and report
scenes.text: Short, regular awareness sessions and a no-blame reporting channel. Staff catch the fake login, the text, the call and the prompt that keeps coming back.

scenes.title: Process: routines, not one person's judgment
scenes.text: A call-back to a known number and a second approver before any payment or bank-detail change stop the payment tricks.

scenes.title: Technology: tools that block or limit the damage
scenes.text: Email filtering, phishing-resistant MFA, least privilege, offline backups. The filter stops the mail faking our own address; MFA stops the guessed password. One click is not a disaster: the layers cover each other's holes.
